protagonist.fact: By the end, she chooses to begin living — opens windows, wears her good dress, stops saving life for a future
protagonist.evidence: "She opened the sunroom windows... She hung her good dress where she could wear it on any ordinary Tuesday."

cinematic_inference.protagonist_occupation: Conservation Technician / Artifact Restorer at a regional museum
cinematic_inference.body_design: 5'6", medium build with strong forearms and nimble hands; slightly rounded posture and steady, deliberate movement.
cinematic_inference.ethnicity_design: White, Midwestern American. (Deliberate production choice — please confirm this casting decision with the creative team; it is not required by the abstract profile.)
cinematic_inference.hair_design: Dark ash-brown, cut in a practical collar-length bob with a few silver strands at the temples; usually pinned back loosely when working.
cinematic_inference.wardrobe_design: A single coherent wardrobe: conservative-casual day dresses in muted earth tones (solid and small-scale plaid), layered with two soft cardigans (one charcoal, one olive), sensible low-heeled leather shoes, and a well-worn canvas lab smock for studio scenes with shallow pockets and thin latex gloves; a lightweight magnifying visor on a flexible headband as needed.
cinematic_inference.casting_rationale: A museum conservation technician aligns with the quiet, methodical temperament and modest independence in the profile while providing tactile, cinematic workspaces. Posture is presented as a neutral, production-ready physical trait (not attributed to occupation). The specified ethnicity is an intentional casting decision and should be confirmed with the creative team.

stable_identity: Late 40s–early 50s woman, reserved and careful, financially independent but modest.
Lives alone in a comfortable small-town bungalow near the regional museum; keeps a tidy, book-lined living room and a small herb window-box.
Enjoys quiet domestic routines: early-morning tea, meticulous gardening of a few perennial beds, and evenings mending textiles or reading conservation journals.
director_profile.social_dynamics: Professional relationships are polite and slow-burning: cordial, respectful interactions with the chief curator and registrar; mentorship of a pragmatic intern; gentle, warily warm rapport with a long-time volunteer donor. Social circles are small; trust is earned through competence and consistent courtesy.
director_profile.professional_vibe: Methodical, quietly authoritative at the bench—decisions grounded in evidence and protocol. She is pragmatic about budgets and deadlines, skillful at negotiating object loans and preparing condition reports, and protective of the museum's collection integrity.
director_profile.visual_vibe: Intimate, tactile visuals: close-ups of gloved fingers, layered textures of aged paper/leather/textile, dusty sunlight through high studio windows, muted color palette—earth tones, sepia, and slate blues. Contrasts between soft cardigans at home and the functional smock at work create a visual duality.
credible_worlds: The conservation studio: long bench, magnifying lamps, microscopes, trays of tiny tools, labeled chemical bottles, drying racks and textile frames.
Regional museum offices and small galleries: wood-paneled donor rooms, cramped storage vaults, and a compact registrar's office with rolling racks of framed works.

Small-town environments: a Saturday farmer's market where she buys herbs, a local café where she exchanges polite small talk with the curator, and her tidy bungalow with a backyard workbench for minor craft tasks.
director_profile.parallel_story_rule: Do not make a private religious or family institution the protagonist's employer; keep workplace centred on the regional museum and its professional network while allowing personal faith or family life to appear only in off-duty moments.

occupation_selection.job_title: Conservation Technician / Artifact Restorer at a regional museum
occupation_selection.rationale: This role closely matches the abstract profile: it requires quiet, methodical, precise work and rewards an introspective, careful temperament. It supports modest financial independence and solo-focused work while allowing meaningful, slow-forming relationships with curators, volunteers, interns, and donors—fitting her reserved but capable-of-warmth interpersonal style. Visually and narratively, a conservation studio gives varied, cinematic settings (light-filtered bench work, magnifying lamps, solvents, microscopes, textile frames, small tools) and active scenes (delicate hand restoration, problem-solving treatment decisions, supervising an intern, negotiating loans with a curator, prepping an object for transport) without relying on bureaucratic meetings. Costume and movement play naturally into the wardrobe brief (conservative-casual when off-bench; protective smock/hands-on work visually contrasts her usual cardigans), and the work lets the camera linger on focused gestures and tactile details that reveal inner life while permitting episodic external stakes (exhibit deadlines, contested provenance, donor relations). This choice balances credibility with cinematic range while avoiding obvious stereotypes.
